land.text: the county of Aragon: Ansó, Echo and Canfranc, centred on Jaca

predecessors.note: 'Created by the Carolingians in the late 8th or early 9th century'; the Spanish March page has the Aragon valleys under Frankish overlordship between 794 and 806 and castles set up there 798-802. Cliopatria starts the county in 830.

land.text: the county of Aragon: Ansó, Echo and Canfranc, centred on Jaca

successors.note: 'From the death of Galindo Aznárez II, the county of Aragon was incorporated within the crown of Navarre ... absorbed in 922.' The county later 'formed the core of the Kingdom of Aragon' (Ramiro I held the nucleus in 1043; kingdom-of-aragon, written by another group).

capitals.name: Jaca
capitals.note: The page says the county was 'centered on' Jaca, not that it was formally the capital.

rulers.name: Aureolus (Oriol)
rulers.note: 'The earliest attested local ruler was Oriol (807)'; list '???-809'.

rulers.name: Aznar Galíndez I
rulers.note: 'In 820 Charlemagne's vassal, Count Aznar I, was ejected from the county by his son-in-law.'

rulers.name: Galindo Aznárez I
rulers.note: 'In 844, Aznar's son Galindo was forced to make himself a vassal of Íñigo.'

rulers.name: Galindo Aznárez II
rulers.note: Dies without surviving legitimate sons; the county is absorbed by Navarre.

correction.text: the county of Aragon: Ansó, Echo and Canfranc, centred on Jaca

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 807-829: Cliopatria starts the county in 830, but the Aragon page names Oriol as attested count in 807 and Aznar I from 809 to 820; the same shape as the 830 row is used (3,490 km2). The page names only Ansó, Echo and Canfranc and gives no area, so no ratio.

830-874, 3,490 km2 (Ansó, Echo, Canfranc round Jaca): the same cells as Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Sobrarbe' 825-829 row, which the Sobrarbe page presents as legend. Stands; the page records no territorial growth.
875-910, 3,585 km2: 95 km2 more than 830 (one cell at the Ribagorza edge); the Aragon page records no growth, so the difference is Cliopatria's (unverified: page budget).
911-921, 3,585 km2: unchanged; the county lasts until 922 ('absorbed in 922'), one year past the Cliopatria row.

region.text: the county of Aragon: Ansó, Echo and Canfranc, centred on Jaca

ledger.note: 807: the Carolingian county of Aragon is first attested. 'The earliest attested local ruler was Oriol (807)'; the county was 'created by the Carolingians in the late 8th or early 9th century'. The year is the first attestation, not a founding act.

820: Aznar I is ejected and the county breaks from the Franks. 'In 820 Charlemagne's vassal, Count Aznar I, was ejected from the county by his son-in-law' (García the Bad); the Spanish March page has 'the County of Aragon following suit shortly thereafter in 820'.

region.text: the county of Aragon: Ansó, Echo and Canfranc, centred on Jaca

ledger.note: 922: the county is absorbed by Pamplona. 'Into which it was absorbed in 922'; in 922 the Aragonese also 'secured their own bishopric'.

region.text: the county of Aragon: Ansó, Echo and Canfranc, centred on Jaca

ledger.note: 922: Galindo Aznárez II dies without surviving legitimate sons and the County of Aragon becomes part of the crown of Navarre.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of the Aragon valleys
wars.outcome: 'A number of castles were established in Aragon between 798 and 802' and Navarre and Aragon 'came under Carolingian overlordship between 794 and 806' (Spanish March page). Fought before the county's first attested count (807); no zone is drawn.
wars.note: The span begins before the dossier's start year 807; it is listed so the reviewer sees it was considered.

certainty.note: A valley county of three named valleys; no boundary line is recorded on the page.

sources.title: County of Aragon

notes: Cliopatria's County of Aragon (830-921) has the same cells as its 'Kingdom of Sobrarbe' 825-829 row; the Sobrarbe page presents that kingdom as legend, so the land belongs to this county from 807 (see the kingdom-of-sobrarbe dossier). The county ends in 922, one year after the Cliopatria row. Galindo Aznárez I was a vassal of Íñigo of Pamplona from 844 (Pamplona's ledger carries the vassal_start/vassal_end); before 820 the counts were Frankish vassals (the Franks' ledger, another group). The later Kingdom of Aragon (Cliopatria 1015-1168) grows from this county: Ramiro I held the nucleus in 1043 and received lands in Aragon from his father as early as 1015; not settled here. Not on the page: any territorial growth, Hecho, a 921 date, a union with Sobrarbe and Ribagorza under Sancho III. Names needed in the gazetteer: Ansó, Echo, Canfranc (Jaca exists in the gazetteer).
